newsitem.title: JORDAN: Foreign buying lifts Jordan stocks to 18-mth high.
newsitem.headline: Foreign buying lifts Jordan stocks to 18-mth high.

text.p: Heavy international demand for three Jordanian blue chip firms propelled Amman's official share index on Wednesday to its highest level since late 1995.
Brokers said foreign interest in Jordan Cement, Arab Potash and Jordan Phosphate Mines, which has swept the market out the doldrums in the last two weeks, continued unabated.
The official 60-share Amman Financial Market (AFM) index rose 0.82 percent to 158.92 points in strong trade worth 1.86 million dinars ($2.63 million).
"About 80 percent of the big purchases have been from outside," said broker Ibrahim Odeh from Wataniyeh Financial Services. "Jordan cement in particular is in heavy demand."
Jordan Cement shares, which have gained more than seven percent in just over a week, rose 0.08 dinars to 4.09 dinars after trade worth nearly 600,000 dinars.
Jordan Phosphate Mines stock surged by 4.75 percent to 3.75 dinars in healthy trade. Arab Potash made strong early gains but slipped back to close fractionally down at 6.58 dinars.
Brokers attribute foreign interest on those three stocks to expectations they may issue international shares in the form of Global Depository Receipts (GDRs).

But the market as a whole took heart from the government's belated passing of investment reforms earlier this month, which encouraged firms to raise capital and allowed mutual funds and corporate bonds to be established.
Odeh said Jordan National Bank, which rose five percent to 2.06 dinars, and the Housing Bank were also being carried along on the tide of optimism.
"I think these prices can be sustained," said analyst Mohammad Abdallah of Pearl Consulting. "It's steady and the prices not picking up on small volume, so it's not an artificial rise."
The only stock to lose out in the foreign-inspired rally was Arab Bank, one of the Middle East's biggest financial institutions and often the main focus of action on the Amman bourse.
Shares in the bank, whose foreign ownership stake already exceeds the permitted 50 percent level, slipped 0.50 dinars to 255.50 dinars in invisible trade of just 60 shares.
Overall advancing shares outnumbered losers by 33 to seven while another 10 traded but closed unchanged.
The private Pearl Index of the 45 best-performing shares in terms of turnover and financial performance rose 0.10 percent to 79.79 points, 4.32 percent down from the start of the year.
